input.summary:
Roofs part now builds with no REFUSED and no OFF-PALETTE lines; ./make.sh writes build.nbt (1647 roof blocks placed).
Fixes, all in parts/roofs.mjs: keep boxes for the shell's gable triangles, party wall, tower corner and wall-line air; plot 0 fascia dropped so the grid no longer shifts +1 in x; soffit, verge and contrast set to palette blocks; barn cupola rails placed as spruce fence.
Earlier refusals were largely a grid shift from plot 0's fascia at x -1, not only lock collisions.
left: Plot 0 has no fascia now: on a ridge-along-z gable the fascia sat at x -1 and x 12 and shifted the whole grid. Its long eaves carry a soffit only. If the owner wants the birch trapdoor fascia back, hand-place it at x 0 and x 11 under the eave, inside the plot.

The grid is 97x25x20, not the site's 96x25x19 (no refusals, no shift). Two roof fascias sit off-site: plot 1's back fascia (birch_trapdoor at z 19, x 15..22, y 5) and plot 7's east fascia (spruce_trapdoor at x 96, z 6..17, y 11). Fix: fascia off on those roofs, or pull the eave inside. I did not change them: outside this brief.

Plot 2 dormer uses contrast: false to keep the plan's nether_bricks against the yellow walls (tone 0.22 under the 0.3 check). The tone check otherwise swaps in slate, whose tuff and polished deepslate are off-palette. Owner's call.
Shell B placed 0 blocks in this build, so plot 4-7 roofs have not been tested against their walls. Expect refusals at the plot 4 gable and wing planes, like plot 0 and 1, once shell B lands.

The barn's dormers are dropped (too close to the gable ends) and the notes say so; that is the roof tool's decision, left as is. The cupola rails are spruce_fence, not iron_bars, which the palette lacks.

waste.what: Listing the refused writes: runParts' report keeps only the first 8 refusals, so I built a debug copy of the build library with the slice widened to see all 157.
waste.cost: 1 debug copy of build.mjs plus a driver, about 3 tool calls
waste.tool: runParts report should write every refused cell (or a file next to parts-report.json) and name the roof call or helper that wrote it.

waste.what: Finding which roof call wrote a given cell: I ran each plot 3 roof call alone on a blank Grid and scanned for the block.
waste.tool: a roof dry-run per cell (e.g. mcd roof --dry-run --cell x,y,z) reporting the writer's call, its keep boxes and the shift.

waste.what: The keep boxes for each building (gable triangles, party wall, tower corner, wall-line air) were worked out by hand from the refusal list.
waste.tool: a helper that dry-runs roof() against the grid and returns the owned cells it would write, to feed keep automatically.

waste.what: The off-palette ids came from roof-tool defaults and fallbacks: the oak soffit, the slate contrast swap, stripped_birch_log verges making non-existent _stairs/_slab ids, and iron_bars from the barn cupola. I found each by reading roofs.mjs.
waste.cost: about 20 minutes of source reading across roofs.mjs, roof-presets.mjs and treatments
waste.tool: a palette option on roof() (checked inside materialOf and the rails) that reports each substitution with the call's name; roof() notes should carry it.

waste.what: A grid shift from an eave fascia at x -1 was found only by probing coordinates in the built NBT (the first 8 refusals looked like a one-column offset).
waste.cost: 2 probes, then a blank-grid test to confirm shift [1,0,0]
waste.tool: roof() dryRun facts should report shift and bounds vs the site size, and runParts should error when a part grows or shifts the grid.

companions.task: Check the Queen Anne slate courses at the hip valley and the cross gable where the fishscale wall now meets the eave, after the keep boxes cut the eave cells there, to see whether the gap reads as a gap.
Hand-place the eave fascia on plot 0's long eaves at x 0 and x 11 (birch trapdoors), since the tool's fascia would sit off-plot, and trim the plot 1 back fascia that runs off-site.
